tiling.name: Tiling and Symmetry
tiling.truth: A pattern is a rule you can walk around. Repetition is not decoration — it is a claim that the same thing can happen again, and symmetry is the bookkeeping of which repetitions are the same one.
tiling.description: What survives being repeated. A tile carries a rule; a wall carries the tile; the seventeen wallpaper groups are every way a plane can repeat without contradicting itself. Addressing (array_tutorial) says where a thing goes and colour says what is worth putting there; this sequence is what happens when you do it again.
learning_objectives: A tile is a rule, not a picture
Reflection, rotation and glide as operations on a cell
How a rule on one cell becomes a wall
The seventeen wallpaper groups, and why there are exactly seventeen
tiling.deferred_reason: THE UNBRAIDING, 2026-09-07 (Palle). colour was carrying two threads: a COLOUR thread (Nails, Pillar, Walls, Context_Placed) and a PATTERN thread (Pattern_Foundry, Symmetry_Seventeen), diagnosed by the red-thread pass on 2026-09-03 — 'three of the seven rooms contain no colour argument at all'. The pattern rooms leave for a sequence of their own, joined by Tutorial_Pattern and Array_Patterns from array_tutorial. Evidence they are one sequence: pattern_tile_mirror stands in three of the four (Symmetry_Seventeen joins on vr_tile_editor alone), pattern_tile_4x4 in two, pattern_maker_station in two, vr_tile_editor in two. colour's stated truth — 'context, not wavelength' — now applies to every room in colour.
tiling.notes: Born 2026-09-07 out of colour and array_tutorial. It partly undoes the 2026-08-24 fold that dissolved symmetry into colour's census room — stated as a reversal, not smuggled. NOT named for shaders: there are zero .gdshader files under commons/shaders and two shader-named tokens in the registry, and a sequence should not be named for work that does not exist yet. RENAMED 2026-09-07 from `pattern` to `tiling` at Palle's instruction, to keep it distinct from patterngeneration — 'Shaders & Patterns: The Book of Shaders', 25 maps, which stays OUT of the spine for now. Every artifact in these four rooms is a tile, loom, mill or wallpaper piece, and the sequence ends on the seventeen wallpaper groups, which is the classification of plane tilings. `tiling` names what is built; `patterngeneration` names what is designed.
